title: fix(react): the form-view bridge accepts what the contract accepts (#5652)
body:
Fixes #5652

The spec-bridge's `bridges/form-view.ts` held a **third** hand-written description of the
`FormViewSchema` contract — after #5542's leaf and #5596's two containers — and it had already
drifted. Per the triage ruling on the card, the documented-subset design is **kept** (its
non-declarations are a retirement ledger #3901/#3974 depends on, which a blanket
`Omit<FormView, …>` would erase); what changes is that every drift-prone key's **type is now
bound to the `@objectstack/spec` symbol that owns it** instead of restated, so it cannot drift
again.

## The arm table, re-measured — the card was wrong on two of three rows

Measured with `safeParse` against the installed `@objectstack/spec` on this branch, not copied
from the card. Each control is an assertion in `FormViewWidenedArms.test.ts`, so "the contract
admits this" is a measurement in the suite rather than a claim in a comment.

| key | bridge declared | contract, measured | control |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FormSection.columns` | `number` | `1\|2\|3\|4\|'1'\|'2'\|'3'\|'4'` — string arm admitted, folded to a number by the section schema's own pipe | `'3'` accepted, `3` accepted, **`'5'` rejected** (it is an enum of the four counts, not "any string") |
| `FormViewSpec.columns` | `number` | **`number`, no string arm.** `FormViewSchema` rejects `columns: '3'` at the FORM level while `FormSectionSchema` accepts it at the SECTION level | `columns: 2` accepted, `columns: '3'` rejected on its own path |
| `FormField.dependsOn` | `string[]` | **`string` — a bare name. The array arm is rejected outright** (`expected string, received array`) | bare name accepted, `['objectName']` rejected |
| `FormField.visibleWhen`, `FormSection.visibleWhen` | `string` | `string \| { dialect, source?, ast?, meta? }` with **`dialect` REQUIRED** | string arm accepted, `{dialect:'cel',source}` accepted, **`{source}` rejected** |

Two corrections that change the repair:

- **`FormViewSpec.columns` has no string arm.** The card asked for one; the contract refuses it.
  The existing `number` was already right, so it is bound to the contract rather than widened,
  and the section/form asymmetry is pinned side by side so a future reader does not "align" them.
- **`dependsOn` was inverted, not merely narrow.** The bridge admitted *only* the arm the
  contract rejects and refused the only one it admits — the configuration that makes
  `field-selector` / `dynamic-config` work (#5040). It is declared `DependsOnInput`
  (`@object-ui/types`, framework#4074): the value is forwarded unread into the node slot
  declared with exactly that type and read by `resolveDependsOnFields`, whose parameter is
  exactly that type. The contract's arm is a strict subset, which is what the derivation pin
  asserts — narrowing to the contract's `string` alone would refuse array-authored layouts the
  runtime has always honoured, on the same never-parsed inputs `groups` and `visibleOn` are
  still read for.
- **`{ dialect?, source }` is a different layer's type.** It is the evaluator's
  `FieldRulePredicate` (`@object-ui/core`, ADR-0089), and the contract rejects it — an object
  arm without `dialect` is refused. The arm the contract admits is the spec's own expression
  object, which is what is now declared.

## Declaring an arm is not consuming it

Per the ruling, each widened arm is followed **end to end onto the `object-form` node**, and the
predicates one step further into the evaluator that reads them:

- `columns: '3'` on a section now reaches the node as the **number** `3`. This is the one arm
  that needs a translation: the node's section declares `columns?: 1|2|3|4` and
  `FormSectionContainer` indexes its grid-class map by it — and that container's own header says
  where the fold belongs: *"The normalisation belongs at the seam that parses authored metadata,
  not in the container's props."* This bridge is that seam.
- `dependsOn: 'objectName'` reaches `node.sections[].fields[].dependsOn` verbatim.
- `visibleWhen: {dialect:'cel', source:…}` reaches the node's `visibleOn` slot whole, and
  `evalFieldPredicate` is then asserted to return **both** verdicts (`true` for a matching
  record, `false` for a non-matching one) — a predicate the evaluator cannot read returns the
  *fallback* for every record, which on its own is indistinguishable from a `false`.
- The bare-string arm still works: the widening added, it did not replace.

## One bounded in-place fix, named explicitly

Deriving `fields` surfaced a fourth instance of the same defect class in the same file: a
section's `fields` may be a **bare object-field name** — the spec shorthand the sibling bridge in
this directory already honours (`list-view.ts`'s `mapColumn`: *"Spec shorthand: a bare field name
stands for a default column"*). The form bridge ran it through the object mapper instead,
producing `{ name: undefined }` — a field with no identity — for the most ordinary section a
form can declare. It is now forwarded verbatim, which is what the node's own `fields` slot
admits (`ObjectFormSection.fields: (string | FormField)[]`) and what
`normalizeSectionField` resolves against the object schema (*"(1) string shorthand → build
entirely from the object schema"*). Scope-bounded: same class, same file, correct shape already
pinned by the sibling bridge and the destination type.

**Fixture triage:** `FormViewSpecConformance.test.ts` spelled `dependsOn: ['account']` — the one
arm `FormFieldSchema` rejects. It pinned a shape no spec-valid document can carry, so it is
re-spelled to the contract's arm.

## The derivation pin

`FormViewWidenedArms.test.ts` carries invariant `Equal<…>` pins tying each declared type to the
spec symbol that owns it, plus arm-level `Extends<…>` pins that name the value (`'3'`,
`'objectName'`, `{dialect:'cel',source}`). A future hand-restatement fails whatever it restates
the type to. They are erased at runtime — `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, chained from this
package's `type-check` script, is what checks them.

## Verification — every leg at `ecb98f1e`

```
pnpm vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/react/src/spec-bridge
  Test Files  7 passed (7)   Tests  125 passed (125)      VITEST_EXIT=0

pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check
  > tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json            TYPECHECK_EXIT=0
  (after pnpm --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build      BUILD_EXIT=0 — the test project
   sets "paths": {}, so @object-ui/* resolve through built .d.ts, not sibling sources)
```

Gate union, re-run at `ecb98f1e`, each quoting its own verdict line:

```
check-changeset-presence     EXIT=0  ✅  3 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed … declares 1 changeset(s)
check-changeset-no-major     EXIT=0  ✅  No changeset declares a `major` bump.
check-control-bytes          EXIT=0  ✅  OK (scanned 4902 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)
check-spec-symbol-derivation EXIT=0  ✅  1300 files scanned against 4959 spec export names …
                                     ✅  spec alignment claims: 2 declared deliberate copies …
check-phantom-dependencies   EXIT=0  ✅  Every in-scope import is declared by the package that publishes it.
```

**Lint — declared narrowing.** Run package-scoped (`pnpm --filter @object-ui/react lint`, exit 0)
rather than repo-wide: (1) the population is eslint's own resolution of the package, not a guess
— `--format json` reports **120 files** linted; (2) **0 errors, 354 warnings**, of which the three
changed files hold **0 errors and 20 warnings, all `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`** — the
file's existing dialect (`Record<string, any>`, `(node.sections as any[])`); (3) `eslint.config.js`
declares no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`, so **type-aware linting is not enabled**
and an edit to these files cannot move any untouched file's verdict. CI runs the full farm anyway.

### Reverse verification — five legs, each predicted before it ran

Every leg: mutate → **prove the mutation landed on disk** by grepping the injected *and* removed
text (never an editor exit code) → run the predicted checks → restore → `git diff HEAD --stat`
**empty**. The script carries a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restore, so a timeout mid-mutation cannot
leave the tree mutated.

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `FormSectionSpec.columns` → `number` | type-check RED, vitest GREEN | `TYPECHECK_EXIT=2`, 4 errors (`TS2322` on the `'3'` fixtures, `TS2344` on both pins); vitest 125 passed |
| B | the `columns` fold removed from the mapping | vitest RED, type-check GREEN | `VITEST_EXIT=1`, 1 failed — *folds a string SECTION column count onto the number the node carries*; `TYPECHECK_EXIT=0` |
| C | `dependsOn` → `string[]` | type-check RED | `TYPECHECK_EXIT=2`, 5 errors (`TS2322` bare-name fixtures, `TS2344` coverage + arm pins) |
| D | `visibleWhen` → `string` (field **and** section) | type-check RED | `TYPECHECK_EXIT=2`, 7 errors (`TS2322` object-arm fixtures, `TS2344` both `Equal` pins + the arm pin) |
| E | bare-field-name shorthand un-consumed | vitest RED **and** type-check RED | `VITEST_EXIT=1` — *forwards the spec shorthand for a field*; `TYPECHECK_EXIT=2` `TS2345` (`mapField` refuses `string`) |

**Legs that do not discriminate, and why.** Vitest stays green (125 passed) through A, C and D:
those narrowings are type-only and erased at runtime, so only `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` can see
them. Type-check stays green through B: the node builder is `Record<string, any>`, so removing
the fold is invisible to the compiler and only the value assertion catches it. Neither instrument
covers this repair alone — which is why both halves are pinned. The contract controls
(`safeParse`) do not discriminate on any leg by construction: they pin the contract, not the
bridge.
